full_judgment:
59. On the point of common intention, learned Deputy Attorney-General refers to the case of Sree Mishon Chandra Das vs State 68 DLR (AD) 392, where the Appellate Division observed: when the accused himself admits to his own complicity in the commission of the offence, even though he did not take part in the violence which to led to the death of the victim, he cannot escape his liability which is imputed upon him by section 34 of the Penal Code. Clearly the petitioner and the co-accused all went to the place of occurrence with the common intention of killing the victim and he took part by standing guard while the others dealt the fatal blows. Learned Deputy Attorney-General refers to some other decisions on presumption of guilt against the absconding accused, and on common intention. 

 66. Dr Rafiqur Rahman, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellant Golam Mostafa alias Mostafa in Criminal Appeal No. 56 of 2014 submits that there is no ocular evidence against the accused Mostafa. His name appears in the evidence of PW 32 in a manner, which is not consistent with the video footage. The eyewitnesses, namely, PWs 10, 11 and 22 did also not mention his name nor did they identify him in Court. His name though appears in the confessional statements of the co-accused; those are contradictory with each other and have not been corroborated by any other substantive evidence. The learned Judge of the trial Court convicted him on 'the basis of the uncorroborated confessional statements of the co-accused. It is a well settled principle of law that on mere presumption or on the basis of confessional statements of co-accused, one cannot be convicted and in that view of the matter the conviction and sentence awarded on the accused Mostafa is out and out illegal and liable to be set aside.
